summary: Interstate Tycoon became the game-facing layer for ROUTE, translating standards, scenarios, evidence labels, and infrastructure failures into playable decisions.
why_it_mattered: This made the game a proof surface instead of a side project: every fun choice has to correspond to a real ROUTE claim and expose its evidence level.
next_thread: Keep scenario rules, campaign hooks, and browser playtests tied to gated ROUTE artifacts.

summary: The map atlas started treating national, schematic, and regional maps as gated artifacts that the release and game can reuse.
why_it_mattered: This turned maps from screenshots into release assets with ids, regeneration commands, and verification expectations.
next_thread: Keep every game-facing or public map registered with a map id and gate.

summary: The Beck engine shifted toward stop-first geometry: named stops create bends, transfers, intersections, and spacing rhythm rather than being labels added after line drawing.
why_it_mattered: This created the core schematic grammar for T1/T2/T3: lines cannot cheat through places without stops, and map legibility must come from selected nodes.
next_thread: Replace more hand-authored geometry with stop-chain ordering and stop-driven bend constraints.

summary: T3 stopped being a national spaghetti overlay and became a regional-map problem, with zone plans seeded from routes that pass stop-chain rules.
why_it_mattered: This kept local and feeder routes useful without letting them clutter the national schematic, and it gave each region a concrete stop-authoring queue.
next_thread: Build regional T3 maps with local T1/T2 context and zone-specific stop candidates.

summary: Tier equals promise horizon: T1 is 48h/36h, T2 is 24h/12h, T3 is 6h, and T4 is 1h.
why_it_mattered: This changed tiering from road-importance classification into a service-promise system that can select lines and stops algorithmically from freight promises.
next_thread: Build T2/T3/T4 promise-pair selectors from the same doctrine.

summary: The T1 selector began selecting routes from top national 48h/36h SLA promise pairs, route score, top-city stops, and budget.
why_it_mattered: This made I-40 return because southern transcontinental promises require it, while I-84 became the first line below the 11-line cut.
next_thread: Replace hand-authored Beck T1 chains with selector output after stop-chain ordering is solved.

summary: T2 duplicate-service diagnostics identified US30 and US6 as serving the same parent-trunk pair through the same split anchor.
why_it_mattered: This shifted T2 cleanup from visual taste to explicit duplicate-service policy with keep/merge/demote actions.
next_thread: Apply qualification actions to T2 map rendering without deleting real routes.

summary: The Beck map kept real topology, including the DC beltway loop, while making schematic constraints explicit.
why_it_mattered: This set the design standard: do not hack reality away, but force routes to earn map treatment through stops, bends, and diagnostics.
next_thread: Use stop-first geometry so bends and intersections are created by selected stops.

summary: The optimizer doctrine stack closed: SLA portfolio, Beck renderer contract, route/stop column schema, T2 treatment, T3/T4 access, manifest contract, and role reviews now define how selections must be made and audited.
why_it_mattered: This changed optimizer work from a series of clever slices into a governed system: every future line, stop, map bend, lower-tier bubble-up, and held blocker has a spec owner and review surface.
